## iOS App Maintenance

Free Apple ID signing typically expires after 7 days. When the app won't open after expiration, reconnect the iPhone and press `Cmd + R` in Xcode to reinstall and renew the signing for 7 more days:

```bash
cd /Users/max/Desktop/github/interview
source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 22
npx cap open ios
```

If you're only renewing the signing without changing content, you don't need to rebuild the web artifacts.

If you've modified the blog content, you need to rebuild and sync first:

```bash
cd /Users/max/Desktop/github/interview

source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 16.19.1
MOBILE=1 npm run docs:build

source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 22.22.2
npx cap sync ios
npx cap open ios
```

Then select iPhone in Xcode and press `Cmd + R` to install.

joylyboy/douyin-live-monitor.body:
# Douyin Live Room Start/End Monitor

Automatically monitors a batch of Douyin live rooms. Once a room goes live or goes offline, it pushes a notification to iPhone via Bark. Tapping the notification opens Douyin directly through its URL Scheme (`snssdk1128://live`) and enters the corresponding live room.

## How It Works

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[External timer / GitHub Actions trigger] --> B[Run monitor.py]
    B --> C[Read rooms.txt]
    C --> D[Request live.douyin.com/room one by one]
    D --> E{Page contains m3u8/flv stream address?}
    E -- Yes --> F[Mark as live]
    E -- No --> G[Mark as offline]
    F & G --> H[Compare with last state]
    H --> I[If state changed, send Bark]
    I --> J[Tap notification to open Douyin live room]
```

Detection basis: the `liveStatus` field in Douyin's web SSR also returns `normal` for rooms that are live, so it is unreliable. For offline rooms, however, the count of real stream addresses such as `m3u8/flv/pull_url` on the page is 0, while live rooms contain many. Therefore, "the page contains real stream addresses" is used as the reliable signal for being live. If the page cannot be fetched or is abnormal, no notification is sent this time (to prevent false alarms).

## File Overview

- `monitor.py` — main program: reads rooms.txt, detects going live, sends Bark notifications, and writes state.json.
- `rooms.txt` — the monitoring list. Only edit this file; there is no need to touch monitor.py.
- `state.json` — runtime state (last live status), maintained automatically by the program and already added to .gitignore.
- `add_room.ps1` — script for adding rooms from the local command line, independent of this tool (see below).
- `add_room.py` — Python version of the same functionality (backup).
- `.github/workflows/douyin-monitor.yml` — GitHub Actions workflow (native schedule as a fallback).

## rooms.txt Format

One room per line, comma-separated: "link or identifier, display name":

    https://live.douyin.com/125093611494, 子成老师讲家庭教育
    https://v.douyin.com/1_AyxhJoFkc/, 羽川电商

- The display name may be omitted (short links automatically look up the nickname via sec_uid).
- Supported:
  - Pure numeric room ID / Douyin ID (username)
  - `live.douyin.com/room-ID`
  - `v.douyin.com/xxxx`…

leizongmin/ZeroWeb.description: An experimental cross-platform browser project written in Rust.
leizongmin/ZeroWeb.body:
# ZeroWeb

ZeroWeb is an experimental cross-platform browser written from scratch in Rust, supporting macOS, Linux, Windows, and Android. It delivers two things:

- **`ZeroWebView`**: a web rendering library that can be embedded in other applications
- **`ZeroBrowser`**: a full browser application built on the same core

DOM, CSS, layout, rendering, JavaScript bindings, networking, and security boundaries are all implemented in this repository, mainly relying on Rust components under permissive licenses.

This is also an AI-first engineering experiment: humans are responsible only for solution design, key decisions, and result verification, while almost all of the code is written by AI. We want to see how far AI can advance a complex system like a browser when architectural boundaries, tests, and acceptance criteria are clearly defined.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The project is in an experimental stage and **is not a browser for everyday use**. It is suitable for learning, research, and engineering exploration. For commercial or production use, evaluate the features, security, compatibility, performance, and license risks yourself.

## Why this project

- **Embedding first**: In addition to the browser application, it provides a stable Rust `ZeroWebView` API for direct integration into other applications.
- **Clear license boundaries**: Mainline dependencies prefer permissive licenses such as MIT, Apache-2.0, and BSD, so core capabilities are not constrained by copyleft.
- **Full-stack Rust**: The page engine, host layer, and rendering infrastructure are kept within the Rust ecosystem wherever possible.
- **AI can write, but must be reviewable**: Every change must be explainable, testable, and visible.

## Current status

Status legend: ✅ basic capability is available and covered by tests; 🚧 in progress, not yet complete; ⏳ planned.

| Capability | Status | Current state |
|------|------|------|
| Desktop browser | ✅ | Real windows on macOS / Linux / Windows; multiple tabs, address bar, downloads, context menu, zoom, find in page, bookmarks, history, settings |
| Android browser | ✅ | Kotlin/Compose UI + Rust core; multiple tabs, keyboard and IME input, downloads, notifications, Chinese and English bilingual |
| Multi-process architecture | ✅ | Rendering, image decoding, and compositing run in separate processes; page scripts run only within the rendering process |
| Embedding API `ZeroWebView` | ✅ | Stable API and demo, integrating Service Worker, WASM, and security checks |
| HTML / CSS rendering | 🚧 | About 95.7% of upstream WPT reftests pass (15,888 / 16,606, 2026-11-06) |
| JavaScript and DOM | 🚧 | Dual V8 / QuickJS engines, native DOM bindings, Web Components, Worker, ES Modules |
| Networking, storage, and security | ✅ | HTTP/1.1 and…

mocl1220/ip.description: Automatically collects public preferred IPs and organizes them
mocl1220/ip.body:
Project Overview
--------

This project uses the automation script [`autoip6.py`](https://github.com/mocl1220/ip/blob/HEAD/autoip6.py) to periodically fetch Cloudflare preferred IPv4 and IPv6 addresses from multiple public sources, automatically look up the country each address belongs to, and save them to the [`ip.txt`](https://github.com/mocl1220/ip/blob/HEAD/ip.txt) and [`ipv6.txt`](https://github.com/mocl1220/ip/blob/HEAD/ipv6.txt) files respectively. The script supports deduplication and formatted output, and uses GitHub Actions for scheduled automatic updates.

Usage
--------

1. **Local run**

   - Install dependencies:
     ```sh
     pip install requests ipaddress
     ```
   - Run the script:
     ```sh
     python autoip6.py
     ```
   - After running, the `ip.txt` and `ipv6.txt` files will be generated or updated in the current directory.
2. **Automated run (recommended)**

   - This project has [GitHub Actions](https://github.com/mocl1220/ip/blob/HEAD/.github/workflows/autoip6.yml) configured, which automatically fetches and updates the IP files every hour, with no manual action required.

Output File Description
------------

- `ip.txt`: each line is formatted as `IPv4:8443#country code`, e.g. `104.16.47.90:8443#US`
- `ipv6.txt`: each line is formatted as `[IPv6]:8443#country code-IPV6`, e.g. `[2a06:98c1:3120:c39b:7522:c680:d288:d13c]:8443#US-IPV6`

Data Sources
--------

The script automatically fetches data from multiple public IP sources. For the specific sources, see the `urls` list in the [`autoip6.py`](https://github.com/mocl1220/ip/blob/HEAD/autoip6.py) file.

Notes
--------

- Country codes are looked up via ipinfo.io. If the lookup fails, they are marked as `ZZ`.
- To customize the data sources or port number, modify the [`autoip6.py`](https://github.com/mocl1220/ip/blob/HEAD/autoip6.py) script.

molimao/iota.body:
# IOTA Watch

An open-source, five-language, multi-project monitoring dashboard centered on **IOTA Train at Home**. It supports IOTA, XID / MMM, Quantus, fly.ai, Nosana, Gonka, Akash, io.net, Vast.ai and Golem; each project's inputs, cycles, and data coverage are described separately.

**[Official site](https://iotahome.site) · [My Devices](https://iotahome.site/zh/devices) · [IOTA Lookup](https://iotahome.site/zh/app) · [Network Status](https://iotahome.site/zh/network) · [Blog](https://iotahome.site/zh/blog) · [English](https://iotahome.site/en)**

IOTA Watch is an independent MIT-licensed monitor in English, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Korean and Japanese. IOTA Train at Home (Macrocosmos / Bittensor SN9) is the core project, with ten project pages covering training, mining and compute. Tool pages query records; separate tutorials explain identifiers, fields and troubleshooting. Public projects use public identifiers; io.net and Vast.ai require account connections with read credentials. Those two integrations have mocked validation; real-account validation remains pending.

The screenshot shows miner distribution and network capacity; the figures are official data as of when the screenshot was taken.

## Features

- **Multi-device monitoring**: add, name, and view devices by public Miner ID, filtering by contributing, waiting for tasks, needs checking, and pending confirmation.
- **Earnings records**: today, cumulative, paid, pending payment, frozen, and minimum payment amounts; also shows USD valuations with source and timestamp.
- **Training history**: view training tokens, throughput, and cumulative tokens by day, week, or month; missing data is left as gaps.
- **Network visualization**: regional distribution donut chart, miner count rankings, slot occupancy, task progress, and tier overview.
